plan.title: [framework-gap] scope:complete clause walk requires a quoted token that the clause says must never appear ('never apikey:…')

narratives.Description: At scope:complete, the clause walk reads every quoted literal in an acceptance clause as text the bound file must contain, unless the clause is one of the #6269 removal sentences. A consumer clause that says a docs view shows a person, org or team name and never an api-key id therefore fails, although the shipped code is correct and must hold the api-key prefix to detect it, and the only way through is an operator acceptance-disposition grant. This story sets aside a quoted literal whose operator is a negation (never inverts it), keeps the presence check for phrases that still require the literal, stops an absence phrase from counting as an existence claim in walkOne and in the #3550 behavioral count, and names checked and set-aside spans on each row. Completion, verified-pass resolution and AC pass banking are unchanged on the checked spans.
narratives.Overview:
1. Negated literal. In `classifyQuotedTokenPolarity`, when no removal word is present, a quoted span whose operator is a negation is set aside. It is not a token check and is never inverted to an absence check. The cues are never, not, no, nor, cannot, without, instead of, rather than, and a word ending in `n't`. A cue governs a span before it only when the span comes next, or when exactly one word between them is a display verb from a closed list (show, display, render, print, emit, log, return, contain, include, appear, output, say, write, in their inflected forms). A cue after the span governs it only in the form span, an optional auxiliary (is, are, was, were, must, should, does, do, did, will, can, may, or a word ending in `n't`), not or never, an optional be or been, then a display verb from the same list. A governing cue before a span also covers the next spans joined to it only by a comma, or, and, or nor. Any other word, punctuation, quoted span or code span between ends the rule, so not only, no change to, without breaking, never omit and never fails to keep the presence check. A cue that follows another cue does not govern the span: before the span, a cue preceded by another cue directly or with one auxiliary between (cannot not show); after the span, an auxiliary ending in `n't`, or cannot, followed by not or never. Two negations keep the presence check. The other spans keep the presence check. If no span is left, polarity is `none`. The #6269 removal grammar (a removal word present) is unchanged.
2. Existence guard. In `walkOne`, the positive existence branch (`EXISTENCE_CLAIM`) also requires that `NEGATED_EXISTENCE` does not match and that no span was set aside by item 1. `isExistenceOrQuotedTokenClause` gets the same set-aside guard on its own existence fallback (it already has the `NEGATED_EXISTENCE` guard). A clause with an absence phrase that the path check does not claim, and a clause whose only spans were set aside, then reach the non-adjudicable behavioral row (#4240), never `verified`, and both helpers count such a clause as behavioral. `isBoundArtifactAbsenceClaim` is unchanged (#7188). Stated limit: a clause that makes a positive existence claim about the bound file and has an absence phrase about something else becomes behavioral, so that existence check is dropped rather than verified; the missing-file failure and the bound-file absence failure run earlier and are unchanged.
3. Row detail. A row with set-aside spans names each span and its cue, and names the spans it did check. A presence failure adds that no removal or negation cue governs the missing literal.
4. Completion unchanged. A clause left with no check is decided where it is today: `clauseWalkBlocks` does not block on it, and on `scope:complete` a walk with no `verified` row still needs a green executable run or the #7047 declared-test floor (#4870). Item evidence alone does not admit it. A mixed clause whose checked span is present still yields a `verified` row, so the `empty-pass` to `verified-pass` relabel and the AC pass bank behave as today; that row covers only the checked spans. This fix removes false `failed` rows and false `verified` rows; it adds no admit path.
5. Docs. `content/docs/plan-acceptance.md` (Quoted-token polarity) states the negation rule, the existence guard and item 4.
6. One ordinary story PR: `packages/core/src/verify-ac/clauses.ts`, `packages/core/src/verify-ac/clauses.test.ts`, a `scope:complete` acceptance-walk test, a verify:ac resolution and banking test, `content/docs/plan-acceptance.md`, one `changelog.d/` fragment.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Given the issue clause shape (a view shows a person, org or team name literal and, after never, an api-key literal) bound to a file that holds the name literal and the api-key prefix, when the walk runs, then the row is verified on the name literal and its detail names the set-aside api-key literal and its cue.
- [ ] Given clauses where the literal is negated by never, not, cannot or a word ending in `n't` directly before it, by one display verb between (does not show, never contains), or after it (the literal, then is never shown, or must not appear), when the walk runs, then the literal is set aside and the row is not failed.
- [ ] Given clauses where the literal follows not only, no change to, without breaking, never omit, never fails to show, or a cue with a comma or colon between, when the walk runs, then that literal keeps the presence check and fails when missing.
- [ ] Given a clause with never before two literals joined by or, when the walk runs, then both literals are set aside.
- [ ] Given a mixed clause with a positive literal of at least three characters and a negated one, when the walk runs, then the positive literal is checked (verified when present, failed when missing) and the negated literal is never checked.
- [ ] Given a clause with an absence phrase that names no declared path, bound to a present file, when the walk runs, then the row is non-adjudicable unverifiable, not verified.
- [ ] Given a clause with a positive existence word and only set-aside spans, when the walk runs and when the #3550 behavioral count runs, then the walk row is non-adjudicable unverifiable and the count treats the clause as behavioral.
- [ ] Given a brief whose only clause has every span set aside, no executable acceptance command and no declared test command, when `scope:complete` evaluates the acceptance walk, then it refuses with the zero-verified notice as today; with a declared test command that passes, the #7047 floor admits it as today.
- [ ] Given a mixed clause whose checked span is present and no executable run, when verify:ac runs on an otherwise bank-eligible brief, then the resolution is `verified-pass`, the AC pass bank accepts it as today, and the row detail lists the set-aside literal as not checked.
- [ ] The existing #3826, #4240, #5393 and #6269 tests in `clauses.test.ts` pass unchanged, and `plan-acceptance.md` states the negation rule and the existence guard.
- [ ] Given a clause with two negations in a row before a literal (cannot not show, or a word ending in `n't` then not show) or after it (an auxiliary ending in `n't` then not appear), when the walk runs, then the literal keeps the presence check and fails when missing.
narratives.Constraint:
- Inverting a negated literal into an absence check (the issue first idea; all three seats): the clause is about rendered output, and the code often must hold the literal to detect it.
- Making a negated clause adjudicable unverifiable, as #6269 does for a negated removal: it still blocks derived-rung briefs, which keeps the false stop.
- A whole-clause rule (any cue drops every span): it reaches 177 of 416 presence clauses at the pin, and drops checks the negation is not about.
- The Stop 1 three-word window (all three seats): it reached 29 clauses and dropped literals the clause still requires. The operator rule in item 1 reaches 11 of 416 presence clauses at the pin in a parent probe, each a negated literal (for example not occupied, not debug, does not say drop it).
- An author-side marker that switches polarity: it adds a step for every author and leaves unmarked clauses misread.
- A subject rule for path absence in this issue: two rules were each blocked by a pain audit; the operator split it into #7188 (resume 7092223080).
narratives.UserStory: As a consumer completing a story whose acceptance clause says a view never shows a quoted literal, I want the scope:complete clause walk to set aside a literal that a negation governs, so that correct work completes without an operator acceptance-disposition grant.

3. clauses.ts row detail: name each set-aside span and its cue and the checked spans; a presence failure says no removal or negation cue governs the missing literal (item 3).

5. ## In plain English

The walk mistakes “never show this text” for “this text must occur in the source.” Dropping that unsupported source check is the right direction. **R1–R4 should not bind as written**, however: the proposed fallback can manufacture a verified result from an unrelated “exist,” and the completion gate does not always accept clauses left entirely unverified.

I verified the relevant code at `ff8e3ee6519527e7c6e30ed4f96ba1b306c9e587`. Execution of all three evidence scripts was blocked by `tsx` attempting a sandbox-denied temporary-directory creation; their reproduction results and corpus totals remain parent claims.

## Answers to questions 1–5

1. **The three-word window is proximity, not grammatical governance.** It catches positive requirements such as “not only prints 'ready'” and “must not fail to display 'ready'.” It misses “‘secret’ is never shown,” longer intervening phrases, and `cannot`.
2. **Dropping unsupported checks is sound; the stated downstream guarantee is incomplete.** `clauseWalkBlocks` excuses non-adjudicable rows, but `scope:complete` separately rejects a zero-verified walk without an executable pass. Conversely, one remaining verified token can promote `empty-pass` to `verified-pass` and enable banking.
3. **R2 clears the reported wrong-subject match, but its fallback needs repair.** A direct `PATH does not exist` remains recognizable. Coordinated subjects, parenthetical modifiers, and same-basename paths need explicit limits. P2 can accompany P1 if the shared fallback is covered.
4. **Authors already control quoted literals, but R1 introduces additional accidental or deliberate ways to suppress checks.** Preserve declared-scope, containment, removal-grammar, and defect-description protections. Do not turn skipped checks into verified behavioral evidence. No new author declaration is needed.
5. **One PR is plausible after revision.** Include completion-level regression coverage, not only classifier tests, and distinguish removal of a false token failure from guaranteed completion.

## Findings

### 1. blocks-the-design — R2 can replace a false failure with false verification

**Evidence:** `packages/core/src/verify-ac/clauses.ts:99–103` defines `EXISTENCE_CLAIM` to match `exist`; `walkOne`, at approximately lines 1612–1623, checks that expression before returning behavioral `unverifiable`. `isExistenceOrQuotedTokenClause` at lines 1812–1818 already excludes `NEGATED_EXISTENCE`, exposing inconsistent treatment between the two consumers.

I checked the pinned existence expression against “The other paths do not exist; inspect merge-group-skip.ts.” It matches `exist`.

**Failure mode:** After R2 rejects the unrelated absence phrase, the #7147-shaped clause reaches the positive existence branch and verifies merely because the bound file exists. R3’s explanatory detail does not prevent that outcome. R1 has the same problem when every literal is skipped but the clause still contains an existence-pattern phrase.

**Disposition:** Revise R1/R2 so a discarded negative or unrelated phrase cannot supply the positive existence oracle. Require the #7147 regression to assert **non-adjudicable `unverifiable`, zero verified**, not merely “no failure.” Reuse and reconcile the existing existence classification rather than adding a gate.

### 2. blocks-the-design — The completion-level fallback contradicts the proposed assurance

**Evidence:** `packages/core/src/scope/acceptance-evidence.ts:2068` defines `walkReportsZeroVerified`; `evaluateScopeCompleteAcceptanceWalk`, around lines 2305–2348, refuses such a walk unless an executable oracle or applicable existing exception admits it. The declared-test floor is already available there. `evaluateAcceptanceEvidenceGate` at line 2407 is a separate item-evidence gate.

**Failure mode:** A brief containing only “The view never renders 'apikey:'” loses its sole verified row under R1. Even though `clauseWalkBlocks` permits the resulting non-adjudicable row, completion can still require an executable command or operator grant. Passing item evidence does not automatically discharge this separate refusal.

The original mixed consumer clause may retain its positive token and avoid this boundary; that does not establish the general fallback claimed for R1.

**Disposition:** Correct the completion claim and test the all-skipped case through `evaluateScopeCompleteAcceptanceWalk`. Explicitly retain the existing executable-floor requirement, or make any intended change to that requirement part of the design. Do not imply that item evidence alone provides the handoff.

### 3. blocks-the-design — R1 suppresses positive assertions within its window

**Evidence:** I inspected `classifyQuotedTokenPolarity` and checked the proposed cue/window expression against representative text. Both “not only prints TOKEN” and “must not fail to display TOKEN” match; “TOKEN is never shown” does not.

**Failure mode:** “The view not only prints 'ready'” requires the literal positively, yet R1 drops it. “Must not fail to display 'ready'” does likewise through double negation. Postposed negation retains the original false presence check. These are ordinary clauses, not adversarial punctuation.

**Disposition:** Replace the claim of grammatical governance with a deliberately bounded recognition rule. Exclude affirmative `not only` constructions; treat uncertain double-negation forms as unsupported rather than confidently negated. Decide explicitly whether postposed negation is supported or residual. Lock these cases before binding the mechanism.

### 4. sharpens-framing — Remaining token checks are partial evidence, with real consumers

**Evidence:** `product-first-done-gate/evaluate.ts:1516–1520` promotes an empty pass when any row verifies. `maybeAttachAcPassBank` at line 2560 forwards `verifiedPass: true`; `session/ac-pass-banking.ts:892–895` permits that path with zero executable runs.

**Failure mode:** In “shows 'ready', never 'secret',” checking only `ready` still yields a verified row and can support banking. That is an existing limitation of token verification, but R1 must not describe it as verification of the skipped negative behavior.

**Disposition:** Keep mixed-span checking, but make R3 identify exactly what was checked and what remains behavioral. Add regression coverage for resolution/banking eligibility so this limitation is deliberate rather than inferred from a green row.

### 5. sharpens-framing — The proposed miniature mixed test may exercise no tokens

**Evidence:** `extractQuotedSpans`, `clauses.ts:1282–1294`, admits raw quoted spans only when their length is 3–80 characters.

**Failure mode:** The suggested `"shows 'A', never 'B'"` fixture extracts neither literal. It cannot prove that the positive span remains checked while the negative span is skipped.

**Disposition:** Use literals such as `'allowed'` and `'forbidden'`, and test both presence and absence of the retained literal.

## Existing mechanisms and alternative

The current mechanisms already provide positioned quote spans, closed removal grammar, declared-file scope, containment checks, defect-description exemptions, behavioral non-adjudicability, a completion test floor, and banking predicates. Build on those.

The strongest alternative is source-absence inversion: it provides a deterministic check for actual source-removal requirements. The existing #6269 grammar already serves that case. I reject general inversion because rendered-output requirements can legitimately require the forbidden string in detection code. An explicit source-content requirement would change that verdict.

## Bound remedy
1. Negated literal. In `classifyQuotedTokenPolarity`, when no removal word is present, a quoted span whose operator is a negation is set aside. It is not a token check and is never inverted to an absence check. The cues are never, not, no, nor, cannot, without, instead of, rather than, and a word ending in `n't`. A cue governs a span before it only when the span comes next, or when exactly one word between them is a display verb from a closed list (show, display, render, print, emit, log, return, contain, include, appear, output, say, write, in their inflected forms). A cue after the span governs it only in the form span, an optional auxiliary (is, are, was, were, must, should, does, do, did, will, can, may, or a word ending in `n't`), not or never, an optional be or been, then a display verb from the same list. A governing cue before a span also covers the next spans joined to it only by a comma, or, and, or nor. Any other word, punctuation, quoted span or code span between ends the rule, so not only, no change to, without breaking, never omit and never fails to keep the presence check. The other spans keep the presence check. If no span is left, polarity is `none`. The #6269 removal grammar (a removal word present) is unchanged.
2. Path-absence subject. `isBoundArtifactAbsenceClaim` fails a present bound file only when the bound file is the last named thing (code span, quoted span or path token) before the absence phrase in the same sentence. A named thing with a directory must equal the bound path; a bare file name must equal the bound basename. Otherwise the clause is not a bound-file absence claim. 1. Negated literal. In `classifyQuotedTokenPolarity`, when no removal word is present, a quoted span whose operator is a negation is set aside. It is not a token check and is never inverted to an absence check. The cues are never, not, no, nor, cannot, without, instead of, rather than, and a word ending in `n't`. A cue governs a span before it only when the span comes next, or when exactly one word between them is a display verb from a closed list (show, display, render, print, emit, log, return, contain, include, appear, output, say, write, in their inflected forms). A cue after the span governs it only in the form span, an optional auxiliary (is, are, was, were, must, should, does, do, did, will, can, may, or a word ending in `n't`), not or never, an optional be or been, then a display verb from the same list. A governing cue before a span also covers the next spans joined to it only by a comma, or, and, or nor. ## In plain English

Problem: at `scope:complete`, the clause walk read every quoted literal in an acceptance clause as text the bound file must contain, unless the clause was one of the #6269 removal sentences. A consumer clause that says a view shows a name and never an api-key id therefore failed, because the walk wanted the api-key literal in the source, although the shipped code was correct and must hold the api-key prefix to detect it. The only way through was an operator `acceptance-disposition` grant. The same presence check also verified some negated clauses it never checked, and the existence branch read the word inside an absence phrase as an existence claim.

Accepted solution: a quoted literal is set aside, not checked and never inverted, when a negation is its operator: the negation sits right before it, one display verb away (does not show, never contains), or right after it (is never shown, must not appear); a literal joined to a negated one by or, and or nor is set aside too. Phrases that still require the literal keep the check: not only, no change to, without breaking, never omit, never fails to, and two negations in a row. An absence phrase never counts as an existence claim, in the walk and in the #3550 counting helper. Each row names what it checked and what it set aside. Completion is unchanged: a walk with no verified row still needs a green run or the #7047 declared-test floor, and resolution and banking read only the checked spans. One ordinary story PR in `packages/core/src/verify-ac/` with tests and the `plan-acceptance.md` docs.

Limits accepted: a clause with a positive existence claim and an unrelated absence phrase loses that existence check; a contracted auxiliary with no not or never after the literal keeps the presence check. The path half (an absence phrase about other paths failing the bound file, #7147 clause 7) is split into #7188 by the operator. The design was checked by source reads at the pinned commit and by parent and critic runs of scratch probes; nothing was built.

## What happened

`scope:complete`'s clause walk (#3323) fails a clause because a quoted string in the clause is missing from the source file. The clause asks for that string to be *absent*.

Clause (consumer repo, `story.1840-desk-p5-desk-polish-final`, clause 4, artifact `web/src/components/docs/docs-article-view.tsx`):

> A docs article by an API key shows a person, org or 'DEFT Team' name, never 'apikey:…'.

Output (directive 0.131.0):

```
[failed] clause 4 @ web/src/components/docs/docs-article-view.tsx: ... — expected token(s) missing from web/src/components/docs/docs-article-view.tsx: apikey:…
acceptance verdict (#3497): clause-walk-failed
```

The shipped code is correct. It detects `apikey:` authors and replaces the id with a name, and `docs-article-view.test.tsx` asserts that no `apikey:` text renders. The literal `apikey:…` (with an ellipsis) should not, and does not, appear in the source.

## Expected

The token extractor should skip, or invert, quoted strings that follow a negation ("never", "no", "not", "without", "instead of"). It could also treat an ellipsis inside a quote as a placeholder rather than a literal. Either way, the error should name the matched phrase, so authors can see why the token applied.

## Impact

A correct story cannot complete unless an operator mints an `acceptance-disposition` grant. The only agent-side workaround is to reword the acceptance text, which edits the gate's input to go green (#3156).

Related: #7099 (keyword axis false trigger in `scope:complete`).
